seattle-start.name: Seattle Public Schools later start time
seattle-start.outcome: High school start moved from 7:50 a.m. to 8:45 a.m.; students slept about 34 minutes more per night, and grades in the studied class rose 4.5%
seattle-start.locator: NPR story on the University of Washington study: "every minute counts"
seattle-start.limits: News report of one University of Washington study of about 90 sophomores at two high schools; the researchers couldn't confirm the extra sleep caused the better grades.

california-sb328.name: California Senate Bill 328 school start times
california-sb328.outcome: Public high schools can't start before 8:30 a.m. and middle schools before 8 a.m., with compliance due by July 1, 2022
california-sb328.locator: "Schools must adhere to the new law before July 1, 2022"
california-sb328.limits: News report, not the statute (the legislature's page blocked the fetch); optional early classes are still allowed, and other reporting says rural districts are exempt. A 2018 version was vetoed as one-size-fits-all.

aasm-sleep-divorce.name: American Academy of Sleep Medicine survey on couples sleeping apart
aasm-sleep-divorce.outcome: Over a third of U.S. adults sleep in another room from their partner occasionally or consistently; 45% of men and 25% of women
aasm-sleep-divorce.locator: Survey release: the arrangement is often called a "sleep divorce"
aasm-sleep-divorce.limits: An online survey of 2,005 adults run for the academy; it shows how common the arrangement is, not that it improves sleep or the relationship.

frankfurt-night-flights.name: Frankfurt Airport night-flight ban won in court
frankfurt-night-flights.outcome: No night flights between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m., after two private plaintiffs won urgent applications against the airport's night-flight rules; the City of Offenbach welcomed the ruling
frankfurt-night-flights.locator: City of Offenbach archive: "not to allow night flights between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m."
frankfurt-night-flights.limits: The city's own archive page, written as an interested party; the 2011 ruling was interim pending the Federal Administrative Court, and the ban covers one airport's night hours, not daytime noise.

habit-nurses.name: HABIT trial of nurse-delivered sleep restriction therapy
habit-nurses.outcome: 642 adults; four brief sessions with a practice nurse cut insomnia severity more than a sleep hygiene leaflet, with large effects at 3, 6 and 12 months
habit-nurses.limits: Run in NHS primary care, where the nurse delivered two sessions in person and two by phone; sleep restriction can bring short-term sleepiness and isn't for everyone, so it is done with a clinician.

nice-sleepio.name: NICE recommendation of the Sleepio app for insomnia
nice-sleepio.outcome: A six-week digital CBT-I course at £45 a person, judged more effective than sleep hygiene and sleeping pills; up to 800,000 people in England could benefit
nice-sleepio.locator: "more effective at reducing insomnia than sleep hygiene and sleeping pills"
nice-sleepio.limits: Trade-press report of the NICE guidance, not the guidance itself; NICE asked for a medical check first for pregnant people and those with other conditions, and for more research against face-to-face CBT-I.

va-insomnia-coach.name: Insomnia Coach app from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
va-insomnia-coach.outcome: A free five-week CBT-I training plan with a sleep diary, personal feedback, and 17 sleep tools
va-insomnia-coach.locator: App Store listing: "designed to be used daily for 5 weeks"
va-insomnia-coach.limits: The developer's own store listing; built for veterans but open to anyone; it says it doesn't replace professional care, and the VA's own page for it returned not found.

apple-apnea.name: Apple Watch sleep apnea notification
apple-apnea.outcome: FDA-authorized over-the-counter feature on Series 9, Series 10 and Ultra 2 that flags possible sleep apnea after 10 nights of data within 30 days
apple-apnea.locator: "over-the-counter device to assess risk of sleep apnea"
apple-apnea.limits: News report; the feature screens for risk and isn't a diagnosis, and it needs an expensive watch.

aasm-apnea-undiagnosed.name: American Academy of Sleep Medicine on undiagnosed sleep apnea
aasm-apnea-undiagnosed.outcome: About 30 million U.S. adults have obstructive sleep apnea, and about 23.5 million of them are undiagnosed; CPAP, oral appliances, positional therapy and surgery treat it
aasm-apnea-undiagnosed.locator: "Is it more than a snore?": "Delaying treatment for sleep apnea can lead to more serious health problems"
aasm-apnea-undiagnosed.limits: The prevalence figures come from an older academy-commissioned estimate; the academy advises talking with a medical provider if a bed partner says you snore, not self-diagnosis.

crazy-inc.name: Crazy Inc. points for a full night's sleep
crazy-inc.outcome: Staff who sleep six hours or more on at least five nights a week, tracked by an app, earn points for food in the company cafeteria
crazy-inc.locator: "sleep six hours a night or more"
crazy-inc.limits: A 2018 news story based on Bloomberg reporting about one small wedding-planning firm; no results reported, current status unknown, and tracking staff sleep raises privacy questions.

aetna-sleep.name: Aetna paying employees for seven hours of sleep
aetna-sleep.outcome: $25 for every 20 nights of at least 7 hours of sleep, up to $300 a year, logged by a wearable or by hand
aetna-sleep.locator: "just over a buck for each night"
aetna-sleep.limits: A 2016 news report; no outcome data on sleep, and later reporting describes the threshold differently. Employer sleep tracking raises privacy questions.

nap-ministry.name: The Nap Ministry collective napping experiences
nap-ministry.outcome: Free group naps of 30 to 40 minutes with mats, pillows and blankets, opening with a meditation and closing with a discussion; founder Tricia Hersey published Rest Is Resistance in 2022
nap-ministry.locator: Tricia Hersey article: "advocates for rest as a form of reparations"
nap-ministry.limits: Encyclopedia article, a secondary source; the sessions are about reclaiming rest rather than treating a sleep disorder.

portugal-no-contact.name: Portugal Law 83/2021 duty of no contact after hours
portugal-no-contact.outcome: Employers must avoid calling, emailing or messaging workers outside working hours; breaches are a serious administrative offense
portugal-no-contact.limits: A legal blog's summary, not the law; force majeure is an undefined exception, and the source reports no evidence on sleep.

eu-working-time.name: EU Working Time Directive daily rest and night work rules
eu-working-time.outcome: At least 11 consecutive hours of rest every 24 hours; night workers average no more than 8 hours a day, get free health assessments, and can sometimes move to day work
eu-working-time.limits: The European Commission's summary page; the year is the directive's number (2003/88/EC), recalled rather than read on the page. Member states apply it with derogations, and it applies only in the EU.

northwestern-light.name: Northwestern Medicine study of light during sleep
northwestern-light.outcome: One night in moderate light (100 lux) rather than dim light (3 lux) raised heart rate during sleep and insulin resistance the next morning
northwestern-light.locator: Tips section: if you can see things clearly, it's probably too bright
northwestern-light.limits: Trade-press report of a small lab study of young adults (the university's own page failed to load); it shows a short-term effect, and tips like blackout shades and eye masks are the researchers' suggestions, not tested treatments.

noise-review.name: Systematic review of white and pink noise for sleep (Capezuti and colleagues)
noise-review.outcome: 34 studies of 1,103 adults; 19 reported some improvement, most often for pink noise (9 of 11), but the evidence was weak
noise-review.locator: "there was no strong evidence to support use of auditory stimulation"
noise-review.limits: Most studies had moderate to high risk of bias; no harms reported from short-term use. A common thing people do, with little proof behind it.

paris-noise-radar.name: Paris noise radar for loud vehicles
paris-noise-radar.outcome: A radar on a lamp post in the 20th district measures each passing vehicle's noise and reads its license plate, with fines planned from 2023
paris-noise-radar.locator: "the first noise radar that is able to measure the noise level of moving vehicles"
paris-noise-radar.limits: A 2022 news report from before fines began; it gives no fine amount and no evidence on residents' sleep.

barcelona-superblocks.name: Barcelona superblocks health evaluation
barcelona-superblocks.place: Barcelona, Spain (Poblenou, Sant Antoni and Horta)
barcelona-superblocks.outcome: Residents and workers in all three of the first superblocks reported less noise and better sleep quality after streets were closed to through traffic
barcelona-superblocks.limits: Sleep and noise were self-reported in surveys and focus groups, not measured; the evaluation ran 2018 to 2020 and the authors call it small-scale.

aasm-standard-time.name: American Academy of Sleep Medicine position for permanent standard time
aasm-standard-time.outcome: The academy calls for ending seasonal clock changes and keeping standard time all year
aasm-standard-time.locator: Standard time "aligns best with human circadian biology"
aasm-standard-time.limits: A position statement, not a law; Congress has debated permanent daylight saving time instead, so people reasonably disagree about which clock to keep.
